q: 1. Bitumen felt is used for .....
explain: Bitumen felt is used both as a water-proofing layer (roofs) and as a damp-proof course.

q: 2. Duco paints are .....
explain: Duco is a trade name for nitro-cellulose lacquer paint, i.e. a cellulose paint.

q: 3. In paints, the pigment is responsible for .....
explain: Pigments give the paint its colour (and opacity).

q: 4. A volatile substance added to a paint to make its application easy and smooth, is known as
explain: A solvent (thinner) is a volatile liquid that reduces paint viscosity for smoother application, evaporating afterward.

q: 5. Pigments are available in the form of
explain: Pigments are typically supplied as fine powders, later mixed with a vehicle to form paint.

q: 6. The most commonly used base for timber painting, is .....
explain: White lead is the most common base for painting woodwork.

q: 7. The most important constituent of varnish, is
explain: Resin is the essential film-forming ingredient of varnish, giving it its glossy, protective finish.

q: 8. The commonly used base for iron and steel work, is .....
explain: Red lead has anti-corrosive properties and is used as the base (primer) for iron and steel.

q: 9. Most commonly used solvent in oil paints, is .....
explain: As per the answer key, option a. Note: turpentine is also very widely used as a thinner in oil paints, so this key answer is debatable.

q: 10. Turpentine oil is used in paints as .....
explain: Turpentine is a volatile liquid used as a thinner, which evaporates after the paint is applied.

q: 11. Plastic asphalt is
options: used as a water proofing layer over roof
a mixture of cement and asphalt
explain: Plastic asphalt, being flexible and impermeable, is applied as a waterproofing layer over roofs.

q: 12. Linseed oil is used in paints as .....
explain: Linseed oil is a drying oil that acts as the vehicle (carrier) for pigment, forming a film when it dries.

q: 13. Bituminous fells are used for
explain: Bituminous felts are commonly used as damp-proof courses (DPC) to block rising moisture in walls.

q: 14. Varnish is a transparent or semi-transparent solution of resinous substances in .....
explain: Varnish can be made by dissolving resins in alcohol (spirit varnish), linseed oil (oil varnish) or turpentine (turpentine varnish).

q: 15. The most fire resistant paint are
explain: Asbestos paints are the most fire resistant because asbestos itself is a non-combustible mineral fiber.

q: 16. Plastic bitumen is generally used for
explain: Being pliable, plastic bitumen is well suited to filling cracks and small gaps in construction.

q: 17. PVC stands for .....
explain: PVC is polyvinyl chloride. Option b is the closest to this in the book, and the key gives b.

q: 18. Fracture of asbestos is
explain: Asbestos is unique for its fibrous structure, meaning it breaks into long, thin, flexible fibers rather than shards.

q: 19. The best primer used for structural steel work is .....
explain: Red lead is anti-corrosive, so it is the best primer for structural steel.

q: 20. The vehicle used in bronze paints is usually .....
explain: Bronze paint uses nitro-cellulose lacquer as the vehicle for the metallic powder.

q: 21. The oil/liquid in which base and pigment are dissolved to form paint is called
explain: The vehicle is the liquid medium (usually oil) that carries and binds the base and pigment together in paint.

q: 22. The pigment used in paints for corrosive resistance, is .....
explain: Red lead is a rust-inhibiting pigment, so it is used where corrosion resistance is needed.

q: 23. The material generally not used as extender in paints is .....
explain: Silica, gypsum and talc are extenders (inert fillers). Zinc white is a pigment (base), not an extender.

q: 24. The commonly used thinner in oil paints, is .....
explain: Both naphtha and turpentine are commonly used thinners for oil paints.

q: 25. The paint which gives illumination during nights is called
options: enamel paint door and windows frames
explain: Fluorescent paint glows or is highly visible under low light/night conditions, aiding visibility.

q: 26. The magnesium refractories material can withstand
explain: Magnesium-based refractories (like Magnesite) are basic refractories capable of withstanding extreme furnace temperatures.

q: 27. Spirit varnish generally consists of .....
explain: Spirit varnish is shellac dissolved in spirit (alcohol). Option d is a misprint of 'spirit and shellac', and it is the one the key gives.

q: 28. Oil varnish generally consists of .....
explain: Oil varnish is made by dissolving resin in linseed oil and turpentine.

q: 29. Bitumen paints offer .....
explain: Bitumen paints give a black protective, water-resistant coating rather than a decorative one.

q: 30. The pigment used in paints for corrosive resistance, is
explain: Red lead is the standard anti-corrosive pigment used in primer paints, especially for iron and steel.

q: 31. The main ingredient in the manufacture of glass is .....
explain: Silica (sand) is the main constituent of glass.

q: 32. The type of glass used for the window of bath room and toilets is .....
explain: Ground (frosted) glass is translucent, giving light with privacy.

q: 33. The type of glass used in glazing the north light trusses is .....
explain: Wired glass is strong and holds together if broken, so it is used for north light glazing.

q: 34. The asbestos content in asbestos cement sheets is roughly about .....
explain: As per the answer key, asbestos cement sheets contain roughly 15% asbestos.

q: 35. Polymerization helps to improve the property of
explain: Polymerization forms long-chain molecular structures that enhance strength, rigidity, and elasticity of materials like polymers.

q: 36. The most important constituent of varnish, is .....
explain: As per the answer key, option d. Note: resin is generally the key ingredient of varnish, so the key answer is debatable.

q: 37. Snowcrete is one of the patent forms of .....
explain: Snowcrete (like Snowcem) is a patented water-proof cement paint.

q: 38. The most fire resistant, paints are .....
explain: Asbestos paints are the most fire resistant since asbestos does not burn.

q: 39. To give a brilliant finish the type of varnish used, is .....
explain: Spirit varnish dries quickly and gives a brilliant, glossy finish.

q: 40. The most durable varnish is .....
explain: Oil varnish forms a tough, durable film and is the most durable type.

q: 41. A constituent of paint that helps in quick drying of painted surface is
explain: A drier is added to paint specifically to speed up the oxidation/drying process of the film.

q: 42. The defect in painting caused by excessive moisture vaporizing in back to the film is known as
explain: Blistering occurs when trapped moisture vaporizes and pushes up the paint film from beneath, forming bubbles.

q: 43. An extender is used in paints for easy spreading. Which of the following can be used as extender in paints?
explain: Gypsum is commonly used as an extender in paint to improve spreading and reduce cost, without materially affecting color.

q: 44. A thinner used in distemper is
explain: Since distemper is a water-based paint, water itself is used as the thinner to adjust its consistency.

q: 45. On which type of surface, lacquer paints are applied?
explain: Lacquer paints, which dry very quickly to a hard glossy finish, are commonly applied on structural steel surfaces.

q: 46. Thinner used for oil paint is
explain: Turpentine is the standard thinner used to reduce the viscosity of oil-based paints.

q: 47. The functions of a base in oil paint are
options: it makes the film of the paint hard, durable and more resistant to abrasion
it gets oxidized in drying and forms a thin, tough, adhesive, durable and water proofing film
it provides gloss to the painted surface
explain: The base (typically a metallic oxide) provides body to the paint, giving the film hardness, durability, and abrasion resistance.

q: 48. The paint having white lead or zinc white as base mixed in oil with petroleum spirit and resinous matter is known as
explain: Enamel paint is formed by combining a white lead/zinc white base with oil, spirit, and resin, producing a hard glossy finish.

q: 49. Out of the following, the material which dries quickly is
explain: Polish, being a spirit-based preparation, dries much faster than oil paints, enamel, or varnish.

q: 50. The small area on painted surface enclosed by hairline cracks are known as
explain: Crazing refers to fine hairline cracks that form a network of small enclosed areas on a painted surface.
